original_finding.title: Managed write-lease validation is split from the state mutation that admits the request
original_finding.description: stcontrolRequestTracker authorizes a managed write from a pre-mutateState snapshot, then records the request as in flight in a later serialized mutation.

root_cause.summary: The adapter performs session tombstone checks, outage/draining mode checks, user write-gate checks, and managed-lease checks against a stale read snapshot before entering the serialized state mutation. mutateState then admits the request without revalidating those invariants on the current state, so a concurrent revoker can invalidate the writer fence and the request still crosses it once.
evidence: src/stcontrol.js:934-978 loads a snapshot, cleans/persists expired entries, promotes mode in memory, and checks gate plus lease before entering mutateState.
src/stcontrol.js:980-1000 increments inFlightWrites/inFlightReads and may create a durable session record, but never rechecks loggedOutAt, current mode, current gate, or current lease.
src/stcontrol.js:826-847 can revoke or shrink leases in applyStcontrolActivityLeaseConfirmations inside mutateState after the request-side lease check has already passed.
src/stcontrol.js:500-547 clears all managed leases on the managed->independent flip, but request admission still trusts the earlier managed snapshot.

src/stcontrol.js:901-912 marks a session logged out and deletes its exact lease in mutateState, yet a concurrent request can still reuse that session object and increment inFlightWrites before next().
src/stcontrol.js:1060-1150 establishes snapshot/data-fault write gates in mutateState, but stcontrolRequestTracker checks state.gates[handle] only before the queue boundary.

request_path: snapshot checks -> ensureSessionEnvelope / mode promotion / gate check / lease check
await mutateState -> increment in-flight counters -> next()
dependency_graph.missing_atomic_boundary: The allow/deny decision and the in-flight admission record are split across two different state observations.

race_windows.name: lease-confirmation refresh
sequence: Request snapshot sees a valid managed lease and passes src/stcontrol.js:973-978.
Agent heartbeat applies a newer confirmation snapshot and deletes the handle from state.leases at src/stcontrol.js:832-838.
Original request enters mutateState at src/stcontrol.js:980 and still increments inFlightWrites, admitting one stale managed write.

race_windows.name: mode flip to independent or draining
sequence: Request snapshot still sees mode=managed and skips independent/draining failover logic.
Controller outage handling flips state.mode and clears state.leases in applyStcontrolMode at src/stcontrol.js:518-525.
Original request enters mutateState and proceeds as a managed writer even though Round 28 requires failover to close the managed fence before independent ownership is re-established.

race_windows.name: logout or write-gate race
sequence: Request snapshot sees no loggedOutAt tombstone and no state.gates[handle].
A concurrent logout or snapshot/data-fault freeze updates state inside mutateState.
Original request still increments counters on the same session object and calls next(), so one post-logout or post-freeze mutation can escape.

remediation_plan.strategy: Keep async ownership/quorum lookups outside the serialized section, but move every local authorization predicate that can change inside the queue. The queued mutation must revalidate current session existence/tombstone, current mode, current gate, and current lease before it records the request as in flight and before the HTTP handler is allowed to continue.

steps.change: Extract an admission helper around mutateState that returns a structured allow/deny result instead of mutating and unconditionally falling through to next().

Inside that helper, rerun cleanExpiredSessions/cleanExpiredSnapshotGates and recheck: stale durable session, loggedOutAt, hadSessionEnvelope-without-session, current mode transition, current gate, and exact managed lease match before incrementing inFlight counters.

If the pre-queue snapshot said managed but the queued state now says independent or draining, fail closed and return a retry/relogin response instead of attempting canUseNativeLogin inside the queue. The next request can enter the normal independent ownership path.
Keep the independent-write pendingSyncUsers marker in the same successful admission transaction so the first disaster-mode write remains crash durable.

Add regression tests that deliberately interleave request admission with lease revocation, mode flip, logout, and write-gate establishment, and assert next() is not called once the queued recheck observes the revoke.

remediation_plan.minimal_fix_scope: A minimal correctness patch touches only request admission and its tests. It does not need a state schema migration, and it can preserve the existing durable mutateState behavior before any later performance optimization.

correctness: The finding remains a direct single-writer fence violation: one stale managed mutation can pass after the system has already decided that this node no longer owns the write.

Round 28 requires already authenticated users to remain usable during controller loss, but only after the node has durably switched to independent-mode rules. This race allows a managed-path write to sneak through after the failover decision and before independent ownership proof.
existing_test_coverage: tests/stcontrol-adapter.node.test.mjs:316-374 proves already-stale managed pages are read-only once the durable lease/session state is already revoked.
tests/stcontrol-adapter.node.test.mjs:384-472 proves lease snapshots revoke omitted writers and fence writes at the exact deadline once the revocation is durably visible before the request starts.
tests/stcontrol-adapter.node.test.mjs:548-625 proves snapshot gates block ordinary writes when the gate already exists before admission.
tests/stcontrol-adapter.node.test.mjs:762-799 proves outage mode clears managed leases, but it does not interleave that mode flip with an already admitted request.
missing_regressions: No test currently pauses stcontrolRequestTracker between src/stcontrol.js:973-978 and src/stcontrol.js:980-1000 to simulate a concurrent revoke.
No test proves a concurrent logout tombstone or write gate can stop next() after the request-side snapshot has already passed.

performance.expected_effect: Negligible on top of the current design because mutateState already serializes and durably persists each admission. The fix adds only a second local predicate evaluation inside the existing critical section.
performance.follow_on_note: A later optimization can separate serialization from persistence, but that is orthogonal and already captured by perf-001-6a1c2b9d.

validation_status.details: 14/14 existing adapter tests passed on August 15, 2026, confirming the race is presently an uncovered correctness gap rather than an already failing baseline test.

reassessed_severity.justification: The bug is reachable on the main write admission path, directly violates the intended single-writer invariant, and is specifically exposed during outage, recovery, logout, and snapshot-freeze transitions when the fence matters most.
